issues.quote: He came into the library at thirty-two minutes past ten by my watch.
issues.fact: F6: Bastien Girard came into the library at 10:32 by Félix's watch.
issues.misreading: The sentence never names Girard. The previous referent for 'he' in the surrounding talk is the uncle ('I thought he had dropped something heavy', 'he did not like it'), so a solver could reasonably read the uncle as the one who entered the library at 10:32 and sat with Félix until eleven. That swaps the person.

issues.quote: He had been four years on that watch
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for how long the uncle has owned or carried the repeater.
issues.misreading: 'Four years' is a duration the sheet does not give. A solver may treat it as a fact about the watch's history or the uncle's habits and build inferences on it.

issues.quote: It has given me trouble for ten years and I have never let anyone near it
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Félix's watch showed 20 minutes to nine at nine, 20 to ten at ten, and so on. It says nothing about the watch being unreliable or faulty.
issues.misreading: Calling the watch troublesome for ten years invites the reader to doubt or discount its readings, or to treat it as a known-slow watch whose offset might vary. The sheet gives the readings as plain facts with no such caveat.

issues.quote: I was alone in the library, Inspector, directly under his bench.
issues.fact: The sheet places the thump 'on the floor right above me, in the atelier.' It does not mention a bench or say where in the atelier anything was.
issues.misreading: 'Directly under his bench' adds a specific location for the uncle inside the atelier that the sheet does not give, which could suggest he was at the bench at the time of the thump.
